# Bumpers and skid plate modifications

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove the oil filter hatch, mark bumper holes, drill them out, and secure self-drilling screws with cut screw protectors. [t473]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the oil filter hatch and verify clearance for drilling.
2. Hold the bumper in its normal position without applying inward or outward tension.
3. Mark the center of each mounting hole with a Sharpie while holding the bumper steady.
4. Drill out all four holes using a 1/8" drill bit.
5. [Partial] Screw in self-drilling #8 x 1/2" screws with fender washers on the lowest impact setting to catch the threads.
6. Repeat the screwing process for the remaining three bolts.
7. [Partial] Gather three #10 and 3/4" long screw protectors (note: guide specifies '1/4"' in text).
8. [Partial] Cut approximately one-third of the length off each protector so they sit flush on just the threads.
9. [Partial] Place a cut protector over the head of each bottom bolt.
10. [Partial] Screw a 1/4" washer over the whole assembly to fit tightly down onto the thread sleeve.
11. Wipe the contact area with alcohol to clean the paint surface.
12. Apply a 1/2" x 1/2" square of double-sided tape to the skid, leaving one side exposed.

_Procedure reported by [t473]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-secure-stock-bumper-to-aftermarket-radiator-skid.10083/>_
